correctness.rationale: Under K arbitrary and \(n\ge2\) the semisimple quotient \(K^n\) forces the vertex-color function because all arrows are square-zero and the reduced quotient has no nonzero nilpotents. Solving orthogonal idempotent lifting separately on each arrow establishes the unique conjugating unit \(1+s\), including same-color edge zero and characteristic-two cases. Peirce spaces \(E_i J E_{i+1}\) classify the images of each arrow and suffice for all relations. Disjoint arrow supports make the image ranks additive. The finite-field factors are  \(q^{d(\phi)}\) and \(q^{m_i(\phi)}-1\); a trace of the successor-colored transition matrix yields the displayed total, checked by a root-of-unity filter. An automorphism is precisely a rotation with nonzero forward-arrow scalars. Standalone checker independently exhausts allowed images over (n,q)=(2,2),(2,3),(3,2), validates multiplication and linear ranks, and compares the normal form with the closed trace formula through \(n=5\); no finite enumeration is substituted for the proof.

value.rationale: The complete operator-rank polynomial is a canonical invariant for the full monoid of unital algebra self-maps, across all \(n\ge2\) and finite field orders. It distinguishes all image dimensions, captures all noninvertible degenerations, and is explained by an explicit split vertex-color, lift, and arrow-coordinate classification. The closed total count and the nontrivial asymptotic fraction of invertible endomorphisms add meaningful quantitative structural information not implied by the compared module-homological literature. The main result is an infinite classification rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
